## Body

Lessons from 2026-11-10 (plans 225/226, F162-F185, prime handover far-jackal -> silkworm):
- Merge ritual: every verdict seat must be at the EXACT final head. After a round-2 fix, ask the other seats for a delta-only verdict (b..c, one file, ~10 min), not a new round.
- C34 after round 2: a wrong recorded state, a stalled seat, or a cancelled action that still happens counts as a normal-use correctness bug; cosmetic or rare-own-write cases are named follow-ups. Answer graders' "block or note?" questions before they publish.
- Never send a seat a packet while its compact is held for a memory turn: the packet keeps the turn going and the compact is dropped (F180). If a reviewer stays stuck, spawn a fresh one (same model), move its reviewer/<n> holdings, close its open requests and reissue them with its R1 verdicts and memory.
- The perf seat measures around bounces: relay its exact window to the prime as a bounce hold and pass on its release. Daemon-cost wins need before AND after on the same paths (one 300 s window plus one 10 s /usr/bin/sample each).
- pij delivered does not release holdings for a PR with no Fixes line (plan PRs): release coder/<plan> and reviewer/<n> by hand at merge.
- A PR that commits machine config (e.g. a private LAN endpoint) must be trimmed before any verdict is published; close the old-head requests unanswered and tell graders not to repeat private details publicly.
- When disk falls under shared-build's 25 GiB floor, CI is the Rust proof; prune review worktrees (just pr-freeze --prune) and stale per-worktree targets that have no lock, process or seat.
- End-of-turn pij blocks work for the PM: READYs and FYIs as a final pij block cost no tool call. Verify they ran in spine_events (message.pushed from pij-steady-otter).
